# Investment Memo: JPM (JPMorgan Chase & Co.) — September 26, 2026

**Verdict**: BUY (small, scale-in) | **Conviction**: Medium
**Price Target**: $370 (+8% from current ~$343; bull $400 / +17%, bear $290–220 on hard landing)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

## Investment Thesis

JPMorgan is the highest-quality US banking franchise — best-in-class margins (26.0% op margin, ~23% ROTCE), the widest deposit moat, a defensive β of 0.77, and conservatively guided earnings that beat 6 of 7 quarters (85.7%, +11.7% avg surprise) into a near-term macro wind (steepened +46bp curve, re-tightening Fed lifting NII, improving card losses; FY26 NII guide raised to ~$105.5B). The honest counterweight: the market already capitalizes this quality at a cycle-top multiple (2.6x book vs. 1.2–1.5x peer band) with no margin of safety, while earnings-quality accruals, credit costs, political litigation, and Dimon succession all trend negative. Own it as quality ballast — small, patient, scaled on pullbacks — not as a growth or conviction bet, and respect the 2027 recession tail.

## Key Findings by Domain

- **Macro & Sector**: FAVOURABLE near-term, bear-tilted. Mature oligopolistic sector (aggregate income −19% in 2025); JPM is the only major bank that grew revenue (+3.3% vs. peer median −1.0%) and leads margins. Bear: Fed re-hiking into decelerating growth — "overtightening into stagflation," 2027 recession tail.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM. ~85% US revenue limits sovereign risk; risk is regulated-industry intensity: $5B Trump suit, record €45M BaFin AML fine, chronic recordkeeping violations, first-ever China Blocking Rule invocation. Russia exposure small/winding down (figure unverified).

- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: BUY (not Strong Buy). EPS $20.05 → $27.26 (2028E), ~10.8% CAGR; +8.5% revisions; 23% ROTCE; buyback-driven. Catalysts: Oct 13 Q3 print, Visa Class C monetization, CCAR 2027, AI cost curve ($19.8B tech budget).
- **Quantitative Signals**: BUY (not Strong Buy). Positive: momentum +7.45%, β 0.77, Sharpe 0.55, revisions. Negative: **accruals 0.046 up 4 years**, Piotroski 4/9, alpha ~0 at R²=0.20, 0.63–0.80 complex correlation.
- **Financial Risk**: **LOW (high conviction)**. Net debt −$537B, $1.48T cash, $362B equity; survives −20% revenue shock still profitable (~$31B NI). **Warning**: Z-score "distress"/F-score "weak" are bank-invalid artifacts — do not propagate. Watches: margin compression, wholesale debt +25%, funding-cost sensitivity.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: MODERATE, trending High. Succession instability (Lake exit, untested co-presidents, Dimon 3+ yrs at ~70), CEO/Chair duality, $5B suit + debanking inquiry. Insider selling routine; no active DPA found.

- **Alternative Data**: MODERATELY BULLISH. 6/7 beats, raised NII guide, broad AI hiring, new HQ; **consumer search proxies cooling** (Sapphire −46% off June peak) = Q4 timing risk. Expect Oct 13 beat, not blowout (Q2 beat was fee/tax-driven; NII missed).
- **Short / Contrarian**: **REJECT the short thesis** — earnings real, no manipulation; all forensic alarms are bank-accounting artifacts. The honest bear is a macro trade: 2027 recession → 30–40% earnings cut, multiple to 10–12x (~$180–220). "Not a short — but emphatically not an aggressive buy at cycle-top."

## Bull Case
- Best-in-class franchise gaining share — only major US bank to grow revenue in 2025, #1 margins, widest deposit moat, β 0.77, natural sector consolidator.
- Earnings momentum intact and under-guided — 85.7% beat rate, FY26 NII raised to ~$105.5B, +8.5% revisions, ~11% EPS CAGR, 1.8% yield + buybacks.
- Near-term macro wind — steep positive curve, rising rates ahead of deposit costs, resilient labor (4.1%), improving card losses, fortress solvency.

## Bear Case
- Cycle-top multiple, no margin of safety — 2.6x book vs. 1.2–1.5x band; hard landing re-rates to 10–12x.
- Top-of-cycle tells — accruals up 4 straight years, op income −2.9% on +3.3% revenue, debt +25%, loans +24% into rising card NCOs (3.2–3.4%), insiders distributing; 2026 acceleration is volatile markets revenue, not NII.
- Macro + governance + political tail — 2027 recession odds, succession churn, $5B presidential suit, debanking legislation, #1 fossil-fuel book.

## Key Risks
1. Macro hard landing (overtightening into stagflation) — the single largest risk, skewing above market pricing.
2. NII guidance cut (bedrock line; Q2 beat was fee/tax-driven).
3. Credit crack — card NCOs sustained above ~3.5%.
4. Governance shock — unplanned Dimon transition without a named successor.
5. Political/regulatory escalation — Trump-suit discovery, debanking legislation, AML enforcement pattern.
6. Funding-cost sensitivity from wholesale debt growth.
7. **Data gaps**: no value anchor (Value Researcher timeout); Russia exposure, Zelle status, CET1/LCR, peer multiples unverified.

Watch: Oct 13 Q3 print, card NCOs, Q4 consumer search proxies, Trump-suit discovery, CCAR 2027 buyback authorization.

Even a dismissed suit raises legal spend, management distraction, and opens the door to Congressional/regulatory pressure on bank account terminations. **Financial impact low; franchise/political risk real.**

JPM is the largest US bank on the mainland and continues investing (Shanghai HQ, JV full ownership). China invoked its **Blocking Rule for the first time in May 2026** telling firms to ignore US sanctions; US tariffs/export controls "tripled over five years" (2025 National Security year-in-review). Basel III Endgame capital requirements are "finally being fully implemented in 2026" (industry press), forcing higher capital reserves against a backdrop of elevated RWA.
